evidence.evidenceExists: We instrumented the save-path and collected latency data from 50 synthetic documents.
evidence.evidenceMissing: Synthetic documents may not capture real-world document complexity or concurrent editing patterns.
assumptions: Synthetic document generation is representative of average user content.
The measurement harness itself does not introduce significant overhead.
evidence.uncertainty: We do not yet know whether the measured latency scales linearly or super-linearly with paragraph count beyond 500.
evidence.disproofCriteria: If the same test on real-world documents shows latency at least 50% lower than synthetic tests, the synthetic document assumption fails.

experimentLog.hypothesis: Save latency is dominated by paragraph serialization and exceeds 2 seconds for documents with more than 500 paragraphs.
experimentLog.whyMatters: If confirmed, this validates the user-reported friction and gives us a measurable target for optimization.
experimentLog.expectedResult: Save latency will exceed 2000ms for 500+ paragraph documents.
experimentLog.testPerformed: 50 synthetic documents from 500 to 1000 paragraphs were saved sequentially with timing instrumentation.
experimentLog.actualResult: Save latency reached 2100ms at 500 paragraphs, 3800ms at 750 paragraphs, and 5600ms at 1000 paragraphs.
experimentLog.expectedVsActualDelta: Actual latency was 5-12% higher than expected at each tier; super-linear scaling was observed above 750 paragraphs.
experimentLog.updatedBelief: The problem is worse than initially described. User reports of 2-second saves were conservative. Super-linear scaling suggests an algorithmic bottleneck.
experimentLog.nextAction: Profile individual serialization functions to identify the specific hot path causing super-linear scaling.
